name_note: GTDB R232 places this species in the genus Ruminococcoides as s__Ruminococcoides bromii; the genomes and the published literature use the name Ruminococcus bromii.

sentences.text: Ruminococcus bromii is the primary resistant starch degrader in humans and relies on the amylosome, a specialised cell-bound enzymatic complex.
Cryo-electron tomography showed that this amylosome comprises a constitutive extracellular layer extending toward the resistant starch substrate.
In constipated mice, four Ruminococcus species were tested and R. bromii was most effective, with its pullulanase enzyme key to degrading resistant starch.
That study reported this degradation boosted short-chain fatty acid production and fostered bacteria such as Akkermansia and Bifidobacterium.
